Summary Collaboration Themes: This collaboration bridges the gap between continuous-time stochastic control theory and formal methods for software verification. By modeling proof generation and neural dynamics as stochastic processes, the researchers can apply rigorous stability analysis (ISS, HJB) to ensure the reliability of AI-driven systems. Key synergies include using formal verification to certify neural control policies, applying risk-sensitive control to manage uncertainty in LLM-generated proofs, and leveraging mean field game theory to optimize large-scale verification tasks. The joint effort aims to create 'verifiable AI' systems that are both theoretically robust and practically scalable.
